title: Cross-Tenant Token Ledger Consistency Service
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, idempotent service that validates and repairs cross-tenant token ledgers produced by our ingestion pipelines and provides explainable deltas for billing attribution. Motivation: recent spikes in small token mismatches across short-lived routes caused customer billing discrepancies and support churn. This service sits between the hourly aggregation jobs and the billing exporter: it consumes aggregated token windows, runs deterministic reconciliation checks, and emits correction events plus a human-readable justification for each change.

Scope:
- Input: hourly and 5-minute aggregated ledger windows from analytics_ingest (S3/Parquet + BigQuery materialized views).
- Output: correction events to kafka.topic:billing-ledger-corrections and an audit table ledger_corrections_{date}.
- Requirements: idempotent retry, per-tenant grouping, retention of original ledger snapshot, explainable reason codes (e.g., missing-stream, rounding-delta, model-fallback-pricing), and task-level metrics for SLOs.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Chose a streaming micro-batch runner (Flink job) instead of a nightly batch to surface issues faster and reduce support lag. Trade-off: increased operational complexity vs. faster detection windows.
- Reconciliation strategy: three-stage diff: exact-key match (route+model+version), heuristic match (prefix-based route aliasing), and statistical outlier detection (for sudden multi-tenant deltas). Heuristics documented in Confluence.
- Cost considerations: keep heavy joins in downstream BigQuery views; the service should only perform in-memory diffs for aggregated keys to avoid per-record scans.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Service processes hourly windows with end-to-end latency < 10m for valid windows.
2) Corrections emitted include tenant_id, window_start, original_tokens, corrected_tokens, reason_code, and links to source snapshots.
3) Alerts fire when per-tenant correction rate exceeds 0.1% of usage in a 24h window.
4) PRD + runbook + post-deploy smoke tests merged before release.

Runbook highlights: start/stop job, force reprocess window, how to replay from S3 snapshots, where to find audit tables and dashboards.

Related artifacts: Confluence design (https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INF/Cross-Tenant+Ledger+Consistency), runbook stub (https://confluence.redwood.example/display/OPS/Ledger+Corrections+Runbook).

implementation_steps: Define canonical aggregation schema and snapshot format (parquet schema) and publish to analytics team
Build Flink micro-batch job: windowing, grouping, diff engine, and correction emitter
Add idempotency keys and checkpointing; support replay from S3 snapshot manifests
Create BigQuery audit tables and views for reconciled vs. original ledgers
Publish runbook and add smoke tests to CI (synthetic windows)
Rollout: canary on internal tenants -> 48h validation -> full rollout
Expose correction counts in Console and notify billing export flow
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy heuristics can produce false positives and unnecessary refunds. Mitigation: conservative thresholds for automatic corrections; default to emit-only mode for first 2 weeks.
Risk: heavy joins will spike BigQuery costs. Mitigation: keep service working over aggregated keys and rely on materialized views maintained by analytics infra.
Risk: ordering/replay bugs could duplicate corrections. Mitigation: idempotency keys and sequence numbers in correction events.
